_comment: How the Hearth-Turner's world remembers. One mechanism, two uses -- WORLD.md's
locked reuse note: 'the block-aging registry powering the Turning IS the same
system that runs the unraveling.' These entries are the same ConversionDef shape
the unraveling's bands use, and deliberately so.
The two are NOT the same table, and the difference is the whole character of the
two systems. The unraveling LOOSENS: intact -> loosened -> dry, a world coming
apart because nobody is holding it. The Turning WEATHERS: a thing acquiring its
own history, in order, and never losing it.
So the chains run through every past state rather than jumping to the end. Stone
does not arrive mossy; it is stone, then cobble, then mossy cobble, and a player
walking back through a place they built can read how long ago they were here.
That is what 'keeping every past' means when it is a block and not a grievance.
NOT here on purpose: copper. Vanilla already oxidises copper by random tick, in
four stages, everywhere. Adding rules for it would mean this world's law and
vanilla's fighting over the same blocks, and the visible result would be copper
ageing at a rate neither of them chose.
SAME HARD GUARANTEE as the unraveling: every 'from' is a naturally-generated or
player-neutral vanilla block, and the runtime consults placement tracking before
touching anything. A conversion that could eat a build is a design failure.
